as a short term fix, this is ok

the long term implications are really really unfortunate. It means the security posture of two key features (swap and user namespaces) are in conflict.… we can't make swap enabled secure for tmpfs mounts if user namespaces are enabled.

> as a short term fix, this is ok
> 
> the long term implications are really really unfortunate. It means the security posture of two key features (swap and user namespaces) are in conflict.… we can't make swap enabled secure for tmpfs mounts if user namespaces are enabled.

Thanks for the information @liggitt.

In which environments kubelet would usually run under a user namespace (hence `RunningInUserNS()` will be `true`)? I'm trying to better understand the use-case and the environments that are affected by this.
Am I misunderstanding the detection? Does this trip on a machine on which user namespaces is enabled at all, or only when the kubelet itself is running in a container with user namespaces enabled?

> In which environments kubelet would usually run under a user namespace (hence RunningInUserNS() will be true)? 

- Usernetes (https://github.com/rootless-containers/usernetes) with Rootless Docker/Podman/nerdctl
- kind with Rootless Docker/Podman/nerdctl
- minikube with Rootless Docker/Podman
- Kubernetes inside LXD/Incus (used by Chrome OS)

> Does this trip on a machine on which user namespaces is enabled at all, or only when the kubelet itself is running in a container with user namespaces enabled?

The latter.

> > In which environments kubelet would usually run under a user namespace (hence RunningInUserNS() will be true)?
> 
> * Usernetes ([rootless-containers/usernetes](https://github.com/rootless-containers/usernetes)) with Rootless Docker/Podman/nerdctl
> * kind with Rootless Docker/Podman/nerdctl
> * minikube with Rootless Docker/Podman
> * Kubernetes inside LXD/Incus (used by Chrome OS)

Since these are non-production environments, I think there is no real damage done.

> > Does this trip on a machine on which user namespaces is enabled at all, or only when the kubelet itself is running in a container with user namespaces enabled?
> 
> The latter.

Thanks for clarifying @AkihiroSuda!

> the long term implications are really really unfortunate. It means the security posture of two key features (swap and user namespaces) are in conflict.… we can't make swap enabled secure for tmpfs mounts if user namespaces are enabled.

To circle back on this explicitly: they shouldn't be in conflict, you can still use kubelet + userns + tmpfs no swap you just can't run kubelet itself in userns and do this (and .. that's already a non-production state).

review_comments:
Would you mind adding a log message here, so it would be clear why tmpfs noswap is not being used?
Perhaps something like:
```go
klog.InfoS("Running under a user namespace - tmpfs noswap is not supported")
```
For my education, do you know why this is the case? It's pretty surprising to me that tmpfs mounts can be done under a user namespace, but not with the noswap option.
